title: Review: Series and parallel circuits; Kirchhoff's laws; Electrical power and energy; Resistivity; Potential dividers; EMF and internal resistance
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EL05-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; EL04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; EL08-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; EL08-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EL04-1#N.10a, EL05-1#N.11a, EL06-1#N.10a, EL06-1#N.11, EL04-1#N.9, EL04-uk1#N.12, EL05-1#N.10b, EL06-1#N.7, EL06-uk1#N.9, EL07-1#N.5, EL08-1#N.7a, EL04-1#N.6a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Power
items.clue: Rate of energy transfer, which can be found from I²R.

items.label: Resistance
items.clue: Quantity proportional to the length of a wire and to 1/A.

items.label: emf
items.clue: Energy transferred to each coulomb of charge by the source.

items.label: Short circuit
items.clue: Connection with R = 0, giving a very large current that heats the cell.

questions.stem: Wire X has resistance R and is made of a material of resistivity ρ. Wire Y is made of the same material at the same temperature, but it is half as long as X and has half the diameter of X. What are the resistance and the resistivity of wire Y?

options.text: resistance R, resistivity ρ
resistance 2R, resistivity ρ
resistance 2R, resistivity 2ρ
resistance R/8, resistivity ρ

questions.explanation: R ∝ length ÷ area: the length factor is ½ and the area factor is ¼, so R_Y = (½ ÷ ¼)R = 2R. Same material and temperature, so the same ρ.

questions.stem: A 60 W lamp and a 100 W lamp are both rated for a 230 V supply. They are connected in series across a 230 V supply. Assume each keeps its normal working resistance. Which lamp is brighter?

options.text: The 60 W lamp: it has the larger resistance, and in series both carry the same current.
The 100 W lamp: it has the higher power rating, so it gives more light.
The 100 W lamp: a smaller resistance gives more power, as P = V²/R.
Both are equally bright, as they carry the same current.

questions.explanation: R = V²/P: about 880 Ω for the 60 W lamp, 530 Ω for the 100 W lamp. Same current in series, so P = I²R is larger in the 60 W lamp (about 23 W against 14 W).

questions.stem: A student wants to measure the current in a lamp and the pd across it, but connects the meters the wrong way round. The circuit is: a cell, a voltmeter and the lamp connected in series in a single loop, with an ammeter connected in parallel with the lamp. Both meters are ideal. What does the student observe?

options.text: The lamp is off and both meters read zero, as there is no current in the circuit.
The lamp is off, the ammeter reads zero and the voltmeter reads the emf of the cell.
The ammeter short-circuits the lamp, so a very large current flows through the ammeter.
The lamp lights normally, and the meters show its current and pd as when correctly connected.

questions.stem: Three identical lamps are connected to a supply of negligible internal resistance: lamp A is in series with lamps B and C, which are in parallel with each other. The filament of lamp C breaks. What happens to the brightness of lamps A and B? (Assume each lamp's resistance stays the same.)

options.text: A and B both go out, because the circuit is now broken.
A becomes dimmer and B becomes brighter.
A stays the same and B becomes brighter, because B now carries C's current.
A becomes brighter and B stays the same, because the parallel branch keeps its potential difference.

questions.stem: A copper wire is connected across an ideal battery. The wire is then cooled from 60 °C to 20 °C; its length and cross-sectional area change by negligible amounts. How do the wire's resistance and the current in it change as it cools?

options.text: The resistance increases, and the current decreases.
The resistance and the current both remain the same.
The resistance decreases; the current does not vary.
The resistance decreases, and the current increases.

questions.stem: An unlabelled wire has a mean diameter of 0.32 mm. Its resistance between the clips is 1.72 Ω at a length of 0.20 m and 5.37 Ω at 0.80 m. Resistivities: copper 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m; iron 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m; constantan 4.9 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m; nichrome 1.1 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m. Which metal is the wire most likely made of?

options.text: Copper
Iron
Constantan
Nichrome

questions.stem: A 60 W lamp and a 100 W lamp are both designed to work on the same 230 V supply. Which lamp has the larger resistance when working normally, and why?

options.text: The 100 W lamp, as a higher power needs a larger resistance.
Both are the same, as they are designed for the same supply pd.
The 60 W lamp, as at the same pd a smaller R gives more power.
The 100 W lamp, as P = I²R and it takes the larger current.

questions.explanation: At the same pd, P = V²/R. R = 230²/60 ≈ 880 Ω for the 60 W lamp and 230²/100 ≈ 530 Ω for the 100 W lamp.

questions.stem: Resistors of 3.0 Ω, 6.0 Ω and 8.0 Ω are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance of the combination?

A 15 V supply charges a 12 V battery. They are connected in a single loop, positive terminal to positive terminal, and the total resistance in the loop is 2.0 Ω. What is the current, and which way does it pass through the battery?

options.text: 13.5 A, in at the battery's negative terminal and out at its positive terminal
7.5 A, in at the battery's positive terminal and out at its negative terminal
1.5 A, in at the battery's positive terminal and out at its negative terminal
1.5 A, in at the battery's negative terminal and out at its positive terminal

questions.explanation: Right. Net emf = 15 − 12 = 3.0 V, so I = 1.5 A. The larger emf wins and drives current backwards through the battery: that is charging.

questions.stem: A potentiometer has a uniform resistance track connected across a 9.0 V dc supply of negligible internal resistance. An ideal voltmeter is connected between one end of the track and the sliding contact, which is one third of the way along the track from that end. What does the voltmeter read?
Cells P and Q have the same emf. P has a smaller internal resistance than Q. Each cell is connected in turn to the same lamp. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The lamp is equally bright with each, as both cells have the same emf.
The terminal pd is larger with P, as less pd is lost inside P.
The terminal pd is larger with Q, as more of the emf is across its resistance.
The current is the same with each, as the lamp alone sets the current.

questions.explanation: Current = emf/(R + r) is larger with P, but lost volts Ir is still smaller, so terminal pd = emf − Ir is larger and the lamp brighter.

questions.stem: A copper cable has length 5.0 m and diameter 1.0 mm. The resistivity of copper is 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m. What is the resistance of the cable?
